notes: rounds/tester.py result() reads the tester's result through own_result (filtered by tester) and runs result_refusal (non-Open round, superseded build, a POST to a submitted result) for GET and again under the round lock for POST, giving a submitted result no form on GET; services.record_result updates only the tester's Draft row, else creates one. M1 drops the tester filter in own_result and in the service's update, so another tester's result is shown and their draft overwritten; M4 removes the POST refusal, shows the form for a submitted result (tester_result.html prints the real status) and lets the service update a Submitted row, since creating a second row would hit the unique constraint as a 503. ResultForm.clean requires a Fail observation (no database constraint); M5 raises only the observation's max_length, whose message is set separately and still says 2000. M3 leaves the tester round page's Open-only 'Record result' link in place (navigation, not a guard). M5 also widens the model field and its column in migration 0005_results to 2001, together, because the varchar(2000) column would otherwise refuse the save (a 503) and a model-only change would fail the candidate's makemigrations --check test; pytest-django builds the test database from migrations on every run (no --reuse-db), so the migration edit is seen consistently.
